# 9 The Cold War, 1945–1991

> Written for SHSID from Indexademics (IDX) study guides. Original material by the IDX club; please keep this credit on any copy.

## Definition

The Cold War was a period of **geopolitical tension between the United States and
the USSR and their respective allies**, the **Western Bloc** and the **Eastern
Bloc** — an intense rivalry between two global superpowers, lasting from the end
of the Second World War in **1945** until the **collapse of the USSR in 1991**.

It was an **ideological war**:

| | United States | USSR |
|---|---|---|
| **Ideology** | Capitalism, democracy, individual freedoms | Communism, state-controlled economy, one-party rule |

It **did not involve direct military conflict**.

## Why it stayed cold

Two reasons are given, and they are the whole explanation for the name. The
Second World War had only just ended and **neither side had recovered from it**;
and both sides held **nuclear weapons that neither would use**, because of
**Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)**.

Instead the two powers **competed for influence in Europe, Asia, Africa and Latin
America**, and both **built massive military forces and developed nuclear weapons
that threatened global destruction**.

## The Yalta Conference, February 1945

Its purpose was to **agree a post-war settlement and decide what to do with
Germany**. The figures present were Prime Minister **Winston Churchill**
(Britain), President **Franklin Delano Roosevelt** (United States) and Premier
**Joseph Stalin** (USSR).

Four outcomes followed.

**1. Germany divided into four zones of occupation**, with the USSR, Britain, the
United States and France each controlling one. France was included because
Churchill and Roosevelt forced a role for it.

| Zone | Controlled by |
|---|---|
| **North-west** | United Kingdom |
| **North-east** | USSR |
| **South-east** | United States |
| **South-west** | France |

**2. Berlin divided into four zones** of occupation, among the same countries.

**3. The Declaration on Liberated Europe** — countries freed from Nazi control
could hold **free, democratic elections** to choose their own governments. Stalin
was offered a **sphere of influence in eastern Europe** where communist ideals
would dominate.

**4. The United Nations** — the Allies agreed to set up an organisation dedicated
to **international cooperation and the prevention of war**.

All the leaders committed to **pursuing and putting on trial suspected Nazi war
criminals**, to prevent Nazis from doing further harm.

> The guide labels the first of these outcomes a *Potsdam excerpt* while listing
> it under Yalta. Both conferences are named in the source and it is worth
> keeping the distinction in mind.

## Konrad Adenauer's memoir

**Konrad Adenauer**, the first prime minister of West Germany, records why the
settlement failed in practice:

- The **Potsdam Conference** required Germany to be treated as **a single economic
  unit**, and this **failed**
- The powers agreed that every decision needed **consensus from the Control
  Council** — France, the USSR, the United Kingdom and the United States — and this
  **also failed**, because they refused to listen to one another
- The **four occupation zones drew further apart economically**, hindering
  economic stability after the war, since **each zone pursued its own policy**

The three points are one argument: a rule requiring unanimity among rivals
produced no decisions, and with no joint decisions each zone went its own way.

## Keywords

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **Cold War** | The 1945–1991 geopolitical tension between the United States and the USSR and their allies |
| **Western Bloc** | The United States and its allies |
| **Eastern Bloc** | The USSR and its allies |
| **Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)** | The condition in which both sides hold nuclear weapons neither will use |
| **Yalta Conference** | The February 1945 meeting agreeing the post-war settlement and the division of Germany |
| **Declaration on Liberated Europe** | The agreement that countries freed from Nazi control could hold free, democratic elections |
| **Sphere of influence** | The area of dominance Stalin was offered in eastern Europe |
| **United Nations** | The organisation the Allies agreed to set up, dedicated to international cooperation and preventing war |
| **Control Council** | The four-power body whose required consensus prevented decisions being made |
